newsitem.title: NEPAL: Nepali Congress says will sit in opposition.
newsitem.headline: Nepali Congress says will sit in opposition.

text.p: The Nepali Congress party of outgoing Prime Minister Sher Bahadur Deuba will sit in the opposition after it failed to cobble together a new coalition government, party officials said on Monday.

The announcement cleared the way for Lokendra Bahadur Chand of the centrist Rashtriya Prajatantra Party (RPP), who has already staked his claim, to be invited by King Birendra to form the next government of the Himalayan kingdom.
The Nepali Congress officials said the party had failed to secure the RPP's support for a new coalition.
"We wanted to have a coalition on the party basis (with the entire RPP) not on an individual basis," said Lakshman Prasad Ghimire, chief secretary of the Nepali Congress.

He told Reuters that some RPP members wanted to form a coalition with the Nepali Congress while another RPP faction had supported Lokendra Bahadur Chand as prime minister. "Naturally we opt to sit in the opposition," Ghimire said.
The deadline fixed by the king to submit proposals for a new government expires at 6.00 p.m. (1215 GMT).
